children: Korean Air completed its largest aircraft purchase agreement, ordering 103 Boeing
planes as the carrier modernizes its fleet and expands following its integration with Asiana Airlines.
The order carries a list-price value of $36.2 billion and includes 20 Boeing

777-9 passenger jets, 25 787-10 Dreamliners, 50 737-10 narrow-body aircraft and eight 777-8 Freighters. Aviation consultancy IBA estimates the planes are worth about $12.6 billion after customary industry discounts, Reuters reported.

Korean Air valued the entire investment package at $44.8 billion. That figure includes $8.6 billion for 21 spare engines from GE Aerospace and CFM International, along with a 15-year maintenance agreement covering engines on 28 aircraft.
The agreement adds substantial long-term business to Boeing’s

order book, but much of the revenue depends on aircraft that have not yet received regulatory approval. Of the four models included, only the 787-10 is currently certified for commercial operations. The 737-10 and 777-9 remain in the certification process, while the 777-8 Freighter is still under development. Delivery schedules and cash collections therefore remain exposed to regulatory and production delays.

The order also reinforces demand for Boeing’s next-generation aircraft despite the manufacturer’s continuing operational challenges. It provides additional long-term revenue opportunities for GE Aerospace and GE-Safran joint venture CFM International through engine sales and maintenance services.

Korean Air said the aircraft will support its expansion after absorbing Asiana Airlines while lowering fuel consumption and operating costs. Approximately 80% of the new planes are expected to replace older aircraft rather than enlarge the combined fleet.

The remaining jets could help Korean Air add routes, particularly to destinations in the United States and Latin America. The mix of wide-body aircraft, freighters and narrow-body planes gives the carrier flexibility across long-haul passenger travel, regional service and cargo operations.

The purchase was initially announced in 2025 during South Korean President Lee Jae-Myung’s visit to Washington. Korean Air Chief Executive Cho Won-tae called the finalized agreements an important milestone and highlighted the commercial relationship between South Korea and the United States.
said the transaction emerged from trade discussions between the two countries.

title: Korean Air finalizes record Boeing order for 103 jets
